metadata.title: Profile: Ameya Deshmukh
metadata.note: ai-explainer `profile` modifier. Subject: Ameya Deshmukh. Thesis: measure, don't guess. Claude bookends + Manim evidence beats (projects, not headshots) + PERSON CREDIT card (verbatim links) + name-carrying outro. @HumanitariansAI. Narrator Liam. Every claim verifiable from Ameya's resume + repos (honesty law).

beats.narration_text: Profile — Ameya Deshmukh. This is Liam, for Humanitarians AI. If you want to know one thing about how Ameya builds, it's this: he measures. Not vibes, not hunches — real numbers, before and after. So let's take his work apart and show you.

props.command: claude "profile Humanitarians AI fellow Ameya Deshmukh — what does he build, and how?"
output: AI/ML engineer — production RAG & multi-agent LLM systems

beats.narration_text: Start with the person. Ameya is an AI and machine-learning engineer — a fellow at Humanitarians AI, with a master's from Northeastern. And across everything he ships, one habit repeats. Where most people guess whether a change helped, Ameya measures it. That's the idea this whole profile lands: measure, don't guess.
beats.visual_intent: name card: Ameya Deshmukh · AI/ML Engineer · MS Northeastern · Humanitarians AI fellow; big thesis 'measure, don't guess'

beats.narration_text: Exhibit one: a production retrieval system over six hundred financial disclosure documents. Anyone can wire up a RAG pipeline. Ameya benchmarked his — chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, a cross-encoder reranker — against a ground-truth set, and moved retrieval quality from a mean-reciprocal-rank of zero point six six to zero point eight one. Not 'it feels better.' A number that moved.
beats.visual_intent: RAG pipeline chips; MRR 0.66 → 0.81 as a rising bar; '600 docs, measured end to end'

beats.narration_text: Exhibit two, at Boehringer Ingelheim, as a data scientist. He connected data sources across more than two million records and pushed data quality up by forty percent — then built a LangChain multi-agent system on top of that healthcare data. Big, messy, regulated data, made usable, then made to reason. Again: a measured lift, not a hopeful one.
beats.visual_intent: 2M+ records → data quality +40%; LangChain multi-agent layer on healthcare claims

beats.narration_text: Exhibit three, and this one shows the discipline best. He built a pipeline to test whether members of Congress beat the market. The easy version stops at a headline return. Ameya didn't — he market-adjusted every trade, ran significance tests, and backtested the signal. The honest finding: individually, no edge; only when independent members cluster on the same stock does a small, real one appear. He let the data say no.
beats.visual_intent: congressional signal: market-adjust → significance test → backtest; 'let the data say no'

beats.narration_text: And he doesn't keep it to himself. For Humanitarians AI, Ameya has shipped a run of explainer films — a whole series on how retrieval-augmented generation really works, from chunking and tokenization to reranking, vector search, and caching. Every episode grounded in that same real project, every number on screen traceable. He makes invisible engineering visible.
beats.visual_intent: grid of the RAG-series episode titles; '14 explainers · every number traceable'

beats.narration_text: Underneath all of it is a consistent toolkit: Python and PyTorch, retrieval and reranking, LangChain and multi-agent systems, SQL and data pipelines. But the tools aren't the point. The point is what he does with them — set a baseline, change one thing, and measure whether it actually helped.
beats.visual_intent: skill chips: Python · PyTorch · RAG · LangChain · multi-agent · SQL/pipelines; footer 'baseline → change → measure'

beats.narration_text: So here's the verdict, and it lands on Ameya's side. In a field full of confident guessing, he's an engineer who insists on evidence — measured retrieval, tested signals, honest negatives. That's exactly the person you want owning a production AI system. Measure, don't guess.

artifactLines: Production RAG & multi-agent LLM systems — benchmarked, not assumed.
Ships the work AND teaches it: a full RAG explainer series.
Measures everything — including when the answer is no.

beats.narration_text: If you're hiring for real AI engineering — someone who can build a production system and prove it works — this is who to talk to. Ameya Deshmukh. His code and his write-ups are public; the links are on screen.
beats.visual_intent: PERSON CREDIT card: Ameya Deshmukh · AI/ML Engineer · Humanitarians AI · MS Northeastern; LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/ameya-deshmukh-179945a4 · GitHub: github.com/Ameya-Deshmukh26

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Don't take my word for it — go read the receipts. Open his financial-disclosure RAG repo, find the evaluation numbers, and watch one of his explainers to see how he thinks. That's the fastest way to know an engineer: read what they measured.
